title: Knowt vs Quizlet vs Gizmo
summary: Pick Knowt for free Learn Mode and spaced repetition, Quizlet for a set you already use, or Gizmo for card-and-deck creation if its free import pacing fits.
body_markdown:
Pick Knowt for free Learn Mode and spaced repetition, Quizlet for a set you already use, or Gizmo for card-and-deck creation if its free import pacing fits your routine.


Educato publishes this page and makes one of the apps on it. We list it where it fits, with its limits.


Option Details Source


Knowt Ultra can summarize PDFs, presentations and lecture recordings and generate study podcasts.[Source](https://knowt.com/plans?tab=Student+Ultra) (checked 2026-11-27)


Knowt Basic includes unlimited file creation, collaboration and storage.[Source](https://knowt.com/plans?tab=Student+Ultra) (checked 2026-11-27)


Knowt Learners can create or import flashcards and study using free Learn Mode, practice tests or spaced repetition.[Source](https://knowt.com/learn-mode) (checked 2026-11-27)


Quizlet Plus includes three practice tests and 20 rounds of Learn a month. Plus Unlimited removes those limits and includes textbook solutions.[Source](https://quizlet.com/upgrade?source=signup) (checked 2026-11-27)


Quizlet A free account provides flashcards, practice questions, diagrams and interactive activities.[Source](https://help.quizlet.com/hc/en-ca/articles/360041181691-Subscribing-to-Quizlet) (checked 2026-11-27)


Quizlet Eligible annual subscriptions offer a seven-day trial that converts to a paid year unless canceled.[Source](https://quizlet.com/upgrade?source=signup) (checked 2026-11-27)


Gizmo Unlimited removes the hearts and import-wait limits and includes unlimited AI Tutor and hints. The provider lists weekly and yearly options.[Source](https://help.gizmo.ai/en/articles/15647627-what-do-i-get-with-gizmo-unlimited) (checked 2026-11-27)


Gizmo Free accounts can create unlimited cards and decks. Memorise uses up to 15 hearts and Magic Import has a 20-minute wait between imports.[Source](https://help.gizmo.ai/en/articles/15647627-what-do-i-get-with-gizmo-unlimited) (checked 2026-11-27)

## Knowt vs Quizlet vs Gizmo: which should I choose for my course?


If your class already has a good Quizlet set, start there. If you are building your own set for a cumulative final, Knowt gives you a way to revisit it over time for free. If you like keeping a separate deck for each lecture, Gizmo lets you make as many decks as you want. The difference shows up when you sit down with Tuesday’s notes and Thursday’s quiz is already on the calendar.


### One economics quiz, three ways to prepare


Suppose your instructor will show you an unfamiliar market and ask you to draw what happens after a change. A classmate shares a Quizlet set with accurate definitions of supply, demand and equilibrium. You also have lecture slides on concert tickets and a handwritten graph of the campus coffee market. Before spending an evening moving cards, try answering one question from the slides using only what you remember from the shared set.


Here is an original example. A band announces its last show. More people want tickets at every price, and the venue has already fixed the number of seats it will sell. What happens to the demand curve, the equilibrium price and the number of tickets sold? Sketch the graph, then turn over the card. A useful back reads, “Demand shifts right. With supply fixed at the venue’s capacity, the equilibrium price rises and the quantity stays the same.”


“More demand means more sales” is a plausible wrong answer. It catches the news about the band and misses the constraint on seats. A card that asks only “What is demand?” would let you recite a correct definition and miss the same quiz question tomorrow. Keep that definition if you need it, but add a second card asking which detail in the story prevents sales from rising. Give yourself credit when you can point to the fixed capacity.


Now change just the cause. The band makes no announcement, but tickets get cheaper. Ask whether that price change alone shifts the demand curve. The answer is no. A lower price changes the quantity demanded along the existing curve. Pairing these prompts exposes an easy mistake: treating every increase in the number of people willing to buy at the posted price as a shift. Draw both pictures from memory before looking at either answer.


### Knowt


Knowt’s free Learn Mode, practice tests and spaced repetition are worth comparing with how often you actually use Quizlet’s paid modes. Ultra also makes summaries from PDFs, presentations and recordings, which is relevant if your deck starts as a lecture rather than as finished cards.[Read the product details](https://knowt.com/plans?tab=Student+Ultra) .


For the economics quiz, create or import the cards you actually want to revisit. Try Learn Mode on the definitions, then draw the ticket graph on scrap paper when the scenario comes up. Use spaced repetition for the distinctions you want to remember after Thursday. A reason to consider Ultra would be a recurring need to summarize lecture recordings. A deck you already understand well enough to write yourself gives you little reason to pay for that step.


### Quizlet


Quizlet Free includes cards and practice questions. Plus and Plus Unlimited have different allowances for Learn and practice tests. Look at the renewal terms of an eligible trial, especially if you only expect to use the paid modes during finals.[Read the product details](https://quizlet.com/upgrade?source=signup) .


Look through the shared set for the exact vocabulary your instructor uses. If the course distinguishes “change in demand” from “change in quantity demanded,” check that the backs do too. An accurate set lets study partners quiz each other on the same wording immediately. If most cards give away the answer in the question, staying with the set saves typing but leaves you with editing to do. Try the free flashcards and practice questions before counting how many paid Learn rounds your schedule would use.


### Gizmo


Gizmo’s free plan permits unlimited cards and decks, but Memorise uses hearts and Magic Import has a waiting period. Consider Unlimited only if you run into those limits during a real session. The number of decks alone does not tell you whether the rhythm suits you.[Read the product details](https://help.gizmo.ai/en/articles/15647627-what-do-i-get-with-gizmo-unlimited) .


Imagine you have a short break to import the concert slides and then a separate coffee worksheet. If the break ends before the next import is available, unlimited deck creation does little for that afternoon’s schedule. If you bring in one lecture at a time, the same wait may never interrupt you. Use the interval after the first import to check the axes and the assumptions on each graph card. A mislabeled price axis is worth fixing before you memorize the picture.


### Educato


Best for choosing document-based questions when a deck of short cards leaves longer answers unrehearsed. Limits: full access requires payment. If you already have an effective deck, a separate subscription needs to solve a specific remaining study problem.


The handwritten coffee graph is a reason to consider this option if your professor’s annotations carry the explanation. A slide might show the finished curves while the margin note records which curve moved first. Keep the annotation with the example and ask yourself to reconstruct the sequence. If a classmate has already put that whole explanation on a clean card, opening another app buys you little for this particular quiz.


### Knowt vs Quizlet vs Gizmo?


For students maintaining their own decks, the decision often comes down to how a free account handles mistakes and repeat sessions. Gizmo uses hearts in Memorise. Knowt offers free Learn Mode and spaced repetition. Quizlet offers practice questions on a free account, with separate terms for its paid study modes.


To settle a tie, take the ticket question into your next study break. Note what you had to do before you could attempt it, whether you could explain your mistake afterward, and how you will find it again before the exam. If preparation ate the break, favor the usable set you already have. If preparation was easy but you forgot to revisit the question, choose the review routine you can repeat between quizzes. Keep the graph you drew; it tells you exactly which card needs another turn.
